For procurement and compliance teams · Zambia

Working with AfriScan in Zambia: procurement, local content and data

What the Public Procurement Act, the mining local-content regulations, the drone rules and the Data Protection Act mean when a public body, a state-owned company or a mining house in Zambia buys structure mapping, wayleave surveys or drone work, and what to ask any supplier for. A summary of public rules, last reviewed 27 September 2026, for orientation; it is not legal or tax advice. Proposals are prepared per project.

Send tender documents How we work

In short

Six questions every supplier file in Zambia should answer

Registration

Is the supplier registered on the ZPPA e-GP system, or on the buyer’s own supplier list, and which company, tax and registration documents does your process need at award?

Bidder status

Is the supplier a citizen, local or foreign bidder under the Public Procurement Act, and which citizen partner does it bring where the method requires one?

Mining local content

For a mining buyer, does the supplier count as a local company under SI 68 of 2025, or which local company is it working with?

Drone approvals

If the scope includes drone work, which Zambian company will fly it, and do its ROC, OpSpecs and Air Services Permit cover the job?

Personal data

Who is the controller and who the processor, is the supplier registered with the Data Protection Commission, and where will imagery and results be stored?

Imagery licences

Which imagery will the work use, with what capture dates and licence terms, and is any of it already held by your organisation?

Supplier registration

ZPPA e-GP, and where the main public buyers advertise

Public entities in Zambia buy through the Zambia Public Procurement Authority’s e-GP system. ZPPA’s supplier registration guide (dated 2016) sets out a manual route for foreign suppliers “that have not registered with the relevant authorities in Zambia”: the organisation’s details, its shareholders, its “CEEC Category” and supporting documents, with up to five UNSPSC codes per supplier. Validation follows before the supplier can bid.

State-owned utilities and corridor operators publish their own tenders as well, and large mining houses and private utilities run their own supplier registration and e-tendering. State the company, tax and registration documents your process needs at award in the tender, and the proposal answers each one.

Where public buyers publish

Buyer Portal
All public entities ZPPA e-GP · ZPPA
ZESCO ZESCO tenders
TAZARA TAZARA tenders
Ministry of Mines and Minerals Development MMMD tenders

Some state tenders are open only to citizen and local suppliers, and some accept sealed paper bids only. Read the bidding method and the submission rules in each notice.

The Public Procurement Act

Citizen, local and foreign bidders

The Public Procurement Act 2020 (No. 8 of 2020), as amended by Act No. 17 of 2023, sorts bidders by status and reserves national competition for citizen and local bidders.

Status Meaning in the Act
Citizen bidder For a firm, one “wholly owned by a citizen”
Local bidder “A non-citizen bidder or supplier who is registered to undertake business activities in the Republic”
Foreign bidder A non-citizen bidder not so registered

Goods, works and non-consulting services (s.39). “Participation in open national bidding shall be limited to citizen and local bidders, except that citizen bidders shall be given priority” (s.39(2)), and a winning local bidder “shall partner with a citizen supplier” (s.39(3)).

Consulting services (s.41). Open national selection is limited to citizen and local bidders (s.41(3)), and a local bidder awarded a contract “shall partner with a citizen supplier” (s.41(4), inserted in 2023). International selection is used only where the service is not available from three suppliers in Zambia, where an agreement requires it, or in “a specialised industry”, and a foreign bidder in international selection “shall partner with a citizen bidder”.

Partnering and subcontracting. Foreign bidders partner with a citizen supplier (s.89(1)(h)), and since 2023 foreign and local bidders subcontract a percentage to citizens for procurements of works (s.93). Regulation 20 of the Public Procurement Regulations 2022 requires foreign bidders to subcontract at least twenty per cent of the total value above the simplified thresholds; whether that still applies to services after the 2023 amendment is for counsel.

Preference. The Public Procurement (Preference and Reservation Schemes) Regulations, SI 45 of 2025, gazetted on 27 June 2025, set margins of preference for local suppliers, citizens, citizen enterprises owned by women, youth or persons with disabilities, small citizen businesses and citizen–local joint ventures or subcontracts. Local preference applies only “where a foreign bidder is permitted to participate”.

The Acts

  • Public Procurement Act 2020
  • Public Procurement (Amendment) Act 2023
  • The Citizens Economic Empowerment Act 2006 (Cap. 419) defines citizen-owned, citizen-empowered and citizen-influenced companies; ZPPA’s registration asks for a “CEEC Category”.

What we put in a proposal

The contracting structure for your tender, including any Zambian partner or joint venture, and which registrations are in place for your contract. We do not describe a status we cannot evidence.

Mining local content

SI 68 of 2025: procurement reserved for local companies

The Geological and Minerals Development (Local Content) (Preference for Goods and Services in the Mining Sector) Regulations 2025, SI 68 of 2025, were gazetted on 14 October 2025 and came into force on 1 January 2026. They apply to mining and mining-related companies:

  • Reservation (reg. 4). Within six months, at least 20 per cent of the annual procurement budget is reserved “for a local company involved in the supply or provision of a core mining good or core mining service”, rising to 25 per cent within one year, 35 per cent within two and at least 40 per cent within five.
  • Preference (reg. 5). A margin of preference for local companies.
  • Exclusive reservation (reg. 6). Non-core goods or services “critical to the operation of the mining industry” are “exclusively reserved for a local company”.
  • Who counts. A “local company” is “a citizen empowered company or a citizen owned company” under the Citizens Economic Empowerment Act.

The schedules name core items such as engineering services, geological and geotechnical services and consultancies on core goods and services, and non-core items such as information systems, information technology and communication, and consultancies in non-core goods and services. Which of them covers satellite and drone mapping is a question for counsel. Upstream petroleum has its own preference rule for Zambian goods, services and citizens (Petroleum (Exploration and Production) Act 2008, s.63).

For mining buyers

Ask each supplier how it meets the regulations for your contract: its own local-company status, with evidence, or the local company it works with and that company’s share of the work. The regulations carry penalties for non-compliance by the mining company, so the evidence matters to you.

Drone work

Who may fly, and what to ask for

Commercial drone work in Zambia needs a ZCAA RPAS Operator Certificate with current OpSpecs and an Air Services Permit, every drone needs a Zambian registration and Letter of Approval, and every pilot a ZCAA Remote Pilot Licence. ZCAA guidance adds, for each operation, a special authorisation, a ZCAA inspector on site and Zambia Air Force airspace clearance. The drones must be on the Zambian register and ZCAA’s company form asks for Zambian company papers, so a foreign supplier flies through a Zambian operator with its own ROC.

For evaluation, split any scope into its satellite or desk-based part, which needs no aviation approval, and its drone part, which needs all of them. Ask for the flying company’s ROC and OpSpecs, its Air Services Permit, its insurance and its plan for the special authorisation and clearance on your timeline.

Drone surveys are subject to the ZCAA approvals and Zambia Air Force clearance each operation requires. Afridrone is working towards the ZCAA approvals Zambia requires, and every AfriScan proposal with a drone element names the Zambian company that will fly it.

The client checklist

Eleven points to check with any drone operator before the first flight, from the ROC and Air Services Permit to consent letters and protected places.

The Data Protection Act 2021

Personal data, storage in Zambia and breach notice

Imagery of homes linked to names, census lists or grievance files is personal data: the Data Protection Act 2021 covers location data and anything from which a person “can be directly or indirectly identified” (s.2). What it asks of controllers and processors:

  • Registration with the Data Protection Commission (s.19); the Commission decides within 14 days (s.20), and the certificate is displayed at the principal place of business (s.21).
  • Storage in Zambia. “A data controller shall process and store personal data on a server or data centre located in the Republic” (s.70(1)). The Minister may prescribe categories that may be stored abroad (s.70(2)), and sensitive personal data always stay in Zambia (s.70(3)).
  • Transfers abroad only on the conditions in s.71.
  • Breach notice to the Commissioner within 24 hours, and to the people affected as soon as practicable (s.49).
  • Impact assessments (s.46), a data protection officer (s.48) and retention rules (s.51).

The Data Protection Commission’s 2025 guide to registering data controllers and processors adds that storage abroad, including “A cloud-based system which stores data outside Zambia”, needs “a separate authorization”, that representatives of foreign entities have their own part of the process, and that registration may be refused if the applicant’s entity is not legally registered or authorised to operate in Zambia.

What to put in the contract: the controller and processor roles, where project data will be processed and stored and any Commission authorisation for storage abroad, breach notice, retention and deletion, who may receive results, and the masking of personal and security-sensitive details in deliverables. Our registers carry structure IDs and coordinates rather than names, so names stay in your own systems; whether any layer is personal data for your project is for your data protection officer or counsel. The proposal states the arrangements for your contract.

How we work

From request to proposal

  1. Send the request

    The route or boundary, the widths, the dates and the deliverables, with the tender documents and the portal reference where there is one.

  2. Scope and imagery

    We check which dated imagery exists for the area and reply with the questions we need answered.

Frequently asked questions

Can a foreign supplier bid in a Zambian public tender?

It depends on the method. Open national bidding for goods, works and non-consulting services is limited to citizen and local bidders, with priority for citizen bidders (Public Procurement Act s.39(2)), and open national selection of consultants is limited in the same way (s.41(3)). International selection is used only where the service is not available from three suppliers in Zambia, where an agreement requires it, or in “a specialised industry”, and a foreign bidder in it “shall partner with a citizen bidder”. The tender document states which method applies.

Does SI 68 of 2025 apply to remote-sensing and mapping work?

The regulations reserve a share of mining procurement for local companies in core goods and services, and reserve some non-core goods and services critical to mining exclusively for them. Their schedules list items such as engineering services, geological and geotechnical services, information systems and consultancies. Which category covers satellite and drone mapping is a question for counsel, and the tender or the mining company’s procurement team will say how it applies the rules.

Does a satellite mapping contract raise the drone-approval questions?

No. The ROC, the Air Services Permit, the special authorisation and the Air Force clearance apply only where an aircraft is flown. Where a scope includes drone work, the proposal separates it, names the Zambian company that will fly it and gives its approval details, so your evaluation can treat each part on its own terms.

Where will our project data be stored?

The Data Protection Act requires personal data to be processed and stored in Zambia (s.70), with exceptions only for categories the Minister prescribes, and the Data Protection Commission’s registration guide says storage abroad needs a separate authorisation. Our registers carry structure IDs and coordinates rather than names, and each proposal states the controller and processor roles and where project data will be processed and stored for your contract.

What do you need from us to prepare a proposal?

The route, network or boundary file, the province and district, the widths or zones to report, the date the record must reflect, the deliverables and the deadline. With a tender, send the documents, the portal and the reference number your process uses, and any supplier-registration or data-protection forms.

Preparing a tender or a supplier file?

Send the tender or request-for-proposal documents, the deadline and your supplier forms. The proposal answers each requirement, states the contracting structure for your tender and says which registrations are in place for your contract.
